tdeeScenarios.titleBefore: An estimate of how much your TDEE (
tdeeScenarios.walk: .. added a 10-minute walk after each meal:
tdeeScenarios.stand: .. stood 3 hours more daily instead of sitting:
tdeeScenarios.alreadyAtMax: — You are already at the estimated maximum
tdeeScenarios.source: Based on Fitness Stuff PAL values
tdeeScenarios.infoIntro: All four scenarios start from your BMR and current TDEE. "⇧"/"⇩" shows the difference versus your current TDEE.
tdeeScenarios.formulaWalk:
Fixed addition = 210 kcal/day
(based on roughly 3 × 10-minute walks at ~70 kcal each)
tdeeScenarios.formulaStandTitle: 3 more hours standing instead of sitting
tdeeScenarios.formulaStand:
Fixed addition = 385 kcal/day
(based on the energy difference standing vs. sitting, Fitness Stuff PAL values)
tdeeScenarios.formulaMostActive:
Estimated TDEE at maximum activity = BMR × 1.5 + 600 kcal

Difference shown = (BMR × 1.5 + 600) − Current TDEE
tdeeScenarios.formulaLeastActive:
Estimated TDEE at minimum activity = BMR + 150 kcal

Difference shown = (BMR + 150) − Current TDEE

phase.noPhaseTitle: What are you working toward right now?
phase.noPhaseBody: Choose whether you want to lose weight, build muscle or hold steady — and we adapt your calorie and protein targets to match.
phase.typeLabel: What do you want to do now?

focus.strengthDesc: You lift and want to build or keep muscle mass.
focus.healthDesc: You want to reach a healthy weight with balanced food.

descriptions.cut: Eat below your needs so fat comes off — with enough protein to keep your muscle.
descriptions.bulk: Eat slightly above your needs to build muscle, without adding more fat than necessary.
descriptions.maintenance: Eat around your needs and keep weight stable — good between phases or once you're where you want to be.
descriptions.reverse: Raise calories step by step after a period in deficit, so your body keeps up and the weight doesn't rush back.

macroMode.label: Diet mode
macroMode.hint: The same numbers as the diet mode in your profile. The diet mode splits them across fat, carbs and protein.

phase.strengthNeedsBodyFat: Maximising muscle growth needs your body fat percentage — the diet modes calculate protein against your fat-free mass. It is also needed to calculate how long a cut will take.

bodyFatNeeded.title: Measure your body fat first
bodyFatNeeded.body: Cutting mode calculates protein against your fat-free mass, so it needs your body fat percentage to give the right numbers.

phase.weeksNotice: The suggested length is a guideline — adjust it based on how you respond.
phase.planningLocked: With Premium you get planned length, a progress bar and suggestions for your next period.
phase.planningLockedReverse: With Premium the app raises your calorie target automatically every week until you're back at maintenance — plus planned length and a progress bar.

modal.title: Choose a period
modal.subtitle: We suggest targets based on your TDEE. You can adjust them.
modal.needsTdee: You need to calculate your TDEE before choosing a period.
modal.previewNotice: You are testing as a new user — the period is saved in the sandbox and does not affect your real profile.

history.title: Past periods
history.empty: No completed periods yet. When you end a period it shows up here.
history.upsell: With Premium you also see planned length and how far each period got.

conflict.title: This will end your active period
conflict.body: You have the period "{{phase}}" running. A new target pointing in a different direction will end it — the period is kept in your history.
conflict.confirm: End it and save the target

phase.trackingNotice: Log your food and weigh in regularly during the period — that is how the app can show whether you are following the plan and whether it is working.

tracking.on_track: You are in line with the plan
tracking.ahead: This is going faster than planned
tracking.behind: This is going slower than planned
tracking.too_early: Too early to tell — weight swings with fluid in the first weeks
tracking.needsWeights: Weigh in to see whether the period is working — otherwise the app only knows what you are aiming for, not what is happening.
tracking.needsOneMore: One more weigh-in and the app can show how the period is going.

prep.title: How long will the cut take?
prep.intro: You are at {{current}}% body fat. Enter a target level and weekly rate to get the time.
prep.rateAcceptable: Faster than recommended. The risk of losing muscle along with the fat increases — competitors who placed averaged 0.46%/week (Chappell 2018).
prep.rateAggressive: Considerably faster than any source supports. In Garthe 2011, 1.4%/week produced no gain in fat-free mass at all.
prep.rateClamped: The rate was adjusted to {{rate}}%/week for the calculation.
prep.belowEssential: Below {{limit}}%, body fat is essential — it sits in organs and the nervous system, not as stored energy. This target cannot be reached.
prep.rangeExplanation: The lower figure assumes you keep all your muscle mass. In practice most people lose some, and then it takes longer.
prep.resultDetail: {{fat}} kg of fat to lose · projected end weight {{weight}} kg · about {{perWeek}} kg in the first week
prep.outsideRange: Longer than the {{min}}–{{max}} weeks documented cuts have taken. Consider a higher target level, or split it into stages with a maintenance period in between.
prep.noResult: Cannot be calculated. The target must be lower than your current body fat percentage.
prep.minorAdjustment: Small distance to the target. Body fat measurement carries an uncertainty of a similar magnitude, so treat this figure as a direction rather than an exact answer.
prep.source1: Helms et al. 2014 — rate 0.5–1%/week, length follows your starting level
prep.source2: Roberts et al. 2020 — ≤0.5%/week; documented periods 14–32 weeks
prep.caveat: Both are narrative reviews from competition literature, not controlled studies. No study has compared different lengths against each other — these figures describe what competitors have done, not what is optimal.

calibrationReadiness.title: On your way to calibration
calibrationReadiness.countdown_one: In {{count}} day the app can work out your real TDEE
calibrationReadiness.countdown_other: In {{count}} days the app can work out your real TDEE
calibrationReadiness.almostThere: Soon the app can work out your real TDEE
calibrationReadiness.nextWeighIn: Next step: weigh yourself tomorrow morning, before breakfast. The same time each day makes your weight comparable between days.
calibrationReadiness.nextLogDay: Next step: log everything you eat today — including what was not planned. That is the difference between your real burn rate and a guess.
calibrationReadiness.nextWeekend: Next step: log at weekends too. Weekend days often run higher than weekdays, and leaving them out makes your burn rate look too low.
calibrationReadiness.nextAlmost: Keep this up for a few more days — then the app can work out your TDEE from your own data.
calibrationReadiness.explainer: Calibration compares what you ate with how your weight responded. That makes your TDEE your own — not a formula estimate.
